sections.heading: Current distortion from modulation
sections.text: Vienna rectifier current distortion is caused by: (1) incorrect space-vector modulation at the sector boundaries, (2) insufficient current-loop bandwidth, (3) neutral-point voltage oscillation. Check the modulation algorithm and increase current-loop crossover if below fsw/10.

sections.heading: Neutral-point voltage oscillation
sections.text: The split DC-bus capacitors develop a voltage imbalance. Add a balancing loop that adjusts the modulation to equalize the capacitor voltages. Bandwidth ~ f_ci/10. If oscillation persists, increase the DC-bus capacitance.

sections.heading: Slow settling of DC bus
sections.text: If the DC bus settles slowly after a load step, the voltage-loop bandwidth is too low. Increase kp/ki, but keep f_cv < 2*f_line to avoid current distortion. The Vienna rectifier voltage loop is inherently slow (same as all PFC topologies).

sections.heading: Architecture limit
sections.text: If the Vienna rectifier cannot meet THD or power factor specs, consider: (1) higher switching frequency, (2) interleaved Vienna rectifier, (3) active front-end with full-bridge for bidirectional capability.
